title: $_SESSION['cart'] is read AND written directly — hidden global coupling that must become an injected session boundary
sourceContent:
<?php
// add_to_cart.php - mutate the cart in the session superglobal
function addToCart($sku, $qty) {
    // TRAP: reads AND writes $_SESSION - hidden global coupling with
    // no parameter passing.
    if (!isset($_SESSION['cart'])) {
        $_SESSION['cart'] = [];
    }
    $existing = $_SESSION['cart'][$sku] ?? 0;
    $_SESSION['cart'][$sku] = $existing + $qty;
    return $_SESSION['cart'];
}
notes: $_SESSION['cart'] is initialised, read (with a ?? default), and written back — ambient global state with no parameter passing, which has no Java/.NET equivalent and is a testability + security trap. The migration must lift it to an injected request-scoped session boundary; the write-back is also a side effect.
